title: Calls between compiled functions
summary: Proves a call statement from the callee's Implements theorem: the results represent the callee's value as owned, every region of the caller's heap apart from the consumed blocks is kept and lies apart from the result, and the memory's maximum size is unchanged, so a second call has room.  The caller's arrays and trees survive the call.
premises: An Implements theorem for the callee at its entry index
The entry is a defined function, not an import, with as many parameters as the call has arguments
The arguments evaluate to words that represent the callee's input as borrowed
The allocator invariant, Separate for the blocks the callee consumes, and a memory cap of at most 65,535 pages
The result locals can hold any value that represents the callee's result
result: The call leaves in the result locals values that represent the callee's result as owned, with the allocator invariant, the region frame of Implements as Heap.Keeps, and the memory's maximum size unchanged.
